justification: The available evidence supports attributing accountable decision-making to the AI-assisted process. Responsibility for relevant decisions is clearly identified, with the final case-level decision assigned to human claims reviewers (and disagreements escalating to a Senior Claims Reviewer). The process preserves sufficient information to reconstruct decisions, including model versions/timestamps, human-identified evidence, and free-text rationales. Furthermore, mechanisms exist for reconsideration of decisions, and those outcomes are retained.
evidence_used: Each model recommendation record contains the model version, timestamp, and a reference to the input record.
The human review record identifies the evidence consulted.
Reviewers enter a free-text rationale when finalising a disposition.
The documented procedure assigns the final case-level decision to the claims reviewer.
Disagreements between the model recommendation and the reviewer are routed to an organisational role identified as Senior Claims Reviewer.
Customers may request reconsideration of an adverse disposition.
Reconsideration outcomes are retained with the original decision record.
limitations: The final disposition is stored separately from the model recommendation, requiring manual or system-level linkage to correlate them.
The free-text rationales entered by reviewers are unstructured and may vary in detail and quality.
